Vs.
Member, Labour Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka and others ----- Respondent
full_judgment: 18. It appears that the petitioner trade union got its registration in the year 1971 when the predecessor-in-interest of the respondent No. 4, namely, Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission as was in existence in the territory of Bangladesh, which was set up under Ordinance 27 of 1965, also had the similar functions as those of the respondent No. 4 and the fund of said Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission also comprised of, amongst others, from donations and endowments, income from investment and royalties and receipts from such other source subject to approval of the Government. Thus we find that the Atomic Energy Commission being a research-oriented institution the law does not permit registration of the trade union. But the registration was given mistakenly on the representation of the sponsors of the petitioner union, who represented them as "worker" and "workmen", which mistake has now been detected by the respondent No. 3. The respondent No. 3, therefore, has filed the case before the respondent No. 2 for cancellation of the illegal registration obtained by misrepresentation which attracts clause (b) of section 10(1) of the Ordinance. There is no bar or estoppel against statute but a mistake of law can be cured any time subject to limitation, if any. In the instant case the respondent No. 3 has taken steps for curing mistake in giving registration to the petitioner union on the misrepresentation of the sponsors of the petitioner union.
